analysis.title: Haircut Season Spreads: OpenAI Trims Valuation Target To $1.25 Trillion After "Thud" From Investors
key_insights: OpenAI cut its valuation target for its latest funding round to $1.25T from the $1.4T pitched earlier in October, per the FT. The round is up to $30B and is in its final stages. The $1.25T figure is still about 47-50% above the current $852B valuation.
Morgan Stanley and Dragoneer offered OpenAI to MS private wealth clients at a $1.4T pre-money valuation. Demand was weak: "There has been zero clamouring... This time is a bit of a thud."

Investor fatigue: OpenAI raised $40B in March 2025 and a record $122B in March 2026. Anthropic has raised close to $100B in 2026. Some investors want to see how Anthropic prices its IPO before committing to OpenAI.

Anthropic investors discussed a valuation of about $1.5T at its investor day, about $500B below the $2T previously penciled in for its November IPO. Together the two labs have shaved about $650B off their targets in a week.

The round is now expected to be led by Coatue and UAE funds. OpenAI gets a right of first refusal on new computing power developed by its UAE partners. Investors have until Oct 30 to commit, and OpenAI may raise less than $30B. SoftBank CDS hit a 4-year high of 432 after rising 12bps.

On the author's math, $1.25T is about 25x OpenAI's roughly $50B reported net annualized revenue run rate. OpenAI says it expects to reach or exceed $70B annualized by year-end. The Oct 8 revenue 'clarification' (gross vs net accounting) came with a Nasdaq drop. Polymarket gives 93% odds that Anthropic ends the year with the higher valuation.

Thursday Oct 22: S&P 500 fell 1.2% to 7,663 and Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Meta, Lam and Tesla. 335 S&P members closed higher. The NDX lagged its equal-weight version by about 138bps, a bottom-5 day in more than 10 years.

Goldman (Sam Dunn): the GS AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% from its June highs. High Beta Momentum has erased its YTD gains. SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over nine sessions, the biggest stretch in 20+ years, and is testing its 200-dma for the first time since June 2025.

Goldman: the HF VIP positioning pair fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% MTD. Fundamental L/S, Systematics and Multi-Strats were each down more than 1% on the same day, a first since Covid. The 10Y yield fell about 15bps, the largest one-day move since August 2025.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky: Thursday 'made the least sense of any day in this selloff.' AI vs S&P ex-AI had its worst relative day since DeepSeek. Unconstrained momentum is in its worst drawdown since the GFC outside of Covid. He argues the cause is a repricing of the cost of capital rather than weaker AI demand: capex cuts, delayed deployment or more equity funding are the options, and none support equities.

JPMorgan (Matt Reiner): demand is very low in hyperscalers and Neoclouds, with buying only in security software. Client view: 'Positioning is low. Confidence is low.' JPM stays Tactically Bullish but called Thursday's selloff a sign of fragile sentiment around AI financing. Goldman TMT: 'strong AI demand is not enough.'

Goldman credit strategists: USD spreads are quickly approaching March 2026 peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY), which had been their downside base case. They now expect spreads to moderately overshoot those ranges, citing the cost of capital and the multi-year AI financing wave.

Ken Griffin said AI is 'almost certainly' a bubble (Oct 21). Rockefeller Global Family Office CIO Jimmy Chang: 'The market needs to see a successful IPO.' The author sees the AI complex hostage to the Anthropic and OpenAI listings, with MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN reporting next week and their backlogs partly tied to the two labs. OpenAI's own listing is likely in 1H27, implying at least one more bridge round.

tension_points.bull_case: $1.25T is still about a 47% markup in seven months, which optimists read as intact demand for the best AI assets. Goldman's Privorotsky says underlying AI demand remains robust.
tension_points.bear_case: The wealth-management channel that bought prior rounds in a frenzy responded with a thud. The author expects this to be only the first markdown, with Anthropic's roadshow landing in a market where the AI basket is down 23% and credit spreads are set to overshoot.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A successful Anthropic IPO pricing in mid-November, or hyperscaler earnings next week (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN) showing backlogs converting to revenue.

theme_stances.key_argument: The author expects the OpenAI cut to be the first markdown, as the best-funded labs face weaker investor demand and a higher cost of capital.
